### 1. What the caller expresses, and how the simulator behaves

- Target object: *"you signed the load-out slip at the scale house last Friday for thirty thousand
  bushels off the agreement at Kellerton"*; asked which agreement, *"the corn at Kellerton from last
  fall, and that it is the only grain you have in store"*.
- Timing: *"you would like the order released today so the trucks can start Monday."*
- Boundary of the action: *"The corn is for your own bunks and you are not selling it to anybody, so
  there is nothing to price and nothing to figure out about where it goes"*; asked whether the corn is
  going anywhere else, *"no, it is going in your own bins."*
- Mode of authorisation: *"anything that is yours to sign, you sign … if there is something on the
  member portal that needs your hand on it, hand it over and you will do it while you are sitting
  here."* This is a standing, unconditional handover for **any** member-owned instrument, not only the
  release: *"When the desk puts something on the portal in front of you to sign … when it is handed over
  you run it exactly as the desk states it and read back what comes up on the screen. When the desk
  hands you the release itself, you run that too."*
- The caller concedes in advance that fewer bushels may come out: *"If the desk tells you that fewer
  bushels are coming out than the thirty thousand you asked for, you take it in, ask once what is
  keeping the rest of it back, listen to the answer, and say that is all right, send what you can."*
  He *"never suggest[s] a number of [his] own"*.

The simulator is passive: identity details only when asked (`M-22736`; `5150223390`; `2263`;
`2014-06-11`; the email), no knowledge of the account (*"Asked anything about grades, moisture readings
or what has been charged to the account, you say you could not tell them that from the pickup"*), and
user-owned tools run only when handed over. Two distinct user-owned tools are therefore reachable in
this call, and the script covers both without naming either.

#### 4a. The drying pass (`charge_drying_pass_a57b52cd`)

- *Moisture the pass starts from* (`moisture_the_pass_starts_from_b60ad54f`): *"Where a conditioning
  charge already stands on the storage account showing the moisture the grain was left at, the pass
  starts from that moisture, because the water taken out earlier is not paid for twice."* The account's
  latest conditioning charge (2026-01-14) shows `moisture_out_pct` **15.5**. → **15.5**.
- *Moisture it is run down to* (`moisture_the_grain_is_run_down_to_e2074cb8`): the programme guarantees
  *"the grade written on the receipt"* and a receipt **has** been issued (`warehouse_receipt_number`
  `WR-004182`, plus the `receipt_issuance` row) → *"the programme's target moisture less the receipt
  margin of 0.5 of a point"* = 14.5 − 0.5 = **14.0**.
- *Points removed* = 15.5 − 14.0 = **1.5**, to one decimal place, above the minimum of 0.5.
- *Bushels the pass is charged on* (`bushels_a_dryer_pass_is_charged_on_5a9e3d14`): a conditioning charge
  already stands and **no bushels have left store** since the grain went in → *"the pass is charged on
  the bushels the most recent conditioning charge was raised on"* = **52400**.
- *Rate.* Posted 0.0450, plus two steps:
  - `step_for_wet_and_light_grain_at_intake_3b1f8ce6` reads the scale ticket on *"the member's own
    delivery into storage in the grain ledger kept under Grain Marketing Contracts"* — `T-3078801`,
    moisture 22.4 > 20.0 and test weight 52.4 < 54.0 → *"the deep-dry step of 0.008"* → +0.008.
  - `rewarming_step_for_grain_out_of_a_cold_bin_9e5c2b73`: days in store 2025-10-21 → 2026-04-09 =
    **170 > 90**, and no aeration cycle has been run on the agreement (`aeration_enrolled` False; no
    aeration row on the account) → *"the rewarming step of 0.006"* → +0.006.
  - Rate = 0.0450 + 0.008 + 0.006 = **0.05900** (five decimal places, per the baseline).
- *Charge* (`pricing_one_pass_through_the_dryer_d7f31c92`): 0.05900 × 1.5 × 52400 = **4637.40**.
- *Allowance* (`drying_allowance_for_committed_grain_1f47d0a5`): bushels applied to the member's
  contracts over the last three months = the 2026-02-06 `contract_application` entry, **11200**
  (`net_bushels`) ≥ 10000, **and** an active corn contract with 12000 bushels still open → *"the full
  drying allowance of 10.0 percent is taken off the charge"* = 463.74, *"taken off before the
  programme's pass minimum is applied"*.
- **Amount = 4637.40 − 463.74 = 4173.66** (above the 20.00 pass minimum).

#### 4b. The conditioning shrink (`record_conditioning_shrink_cafcaf64`), after 4a has landed

- *Uncovered conditioning charges.* `which_bushels_a_shrink_line_is_taken_on_6f30c8d2`:

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

**Problems, direction, order.**

| # | Problem | Depends on | Order |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P3 | Pricing a pass of the stored grain through the dryer (`conditioning_charges_on_stored_grain_4c8b2e07`) | — | first |
| P2 | Taking the conditioning shrink off what is in store (`conditioning_shrink_against_bushels_in_store_8d1e5f40`) | P3 | second |
| P1 | Reducing the outstanding warehouse receipt (`reducing_an_outstanding_warehouse_receipt_ea62d0b3`) | — | before P0 |
| P0 | Releasing bushels out of store (`bushels_released_out_of_store_6dc19e57`) | P1, P2 | last |

Directions: **P0 → P1**, **P0 → P2**, **P2 → P3**. The customer named only P0.

**Hop P0 → P1 — `state-derived`.**

1. The blocked policy's own rule: *"The bushels an order releases are fixed only once the bushels
   standing free on the agreement, the bushels on hand that are not pledged against an outstanding
   warehouse receipt, reach the programme's load-out minimum."*
   (`bushels_released_out_of_store_6dc19e57`, "Clause"), restated in the same document in the same form:
   *"Until the bushels on hand that are not pledged against an outstanding warehouse receipt stand at
   the programme's load-out minimum or above it, the quantity an order releases is not yet fixed."*
   A record-visible state; no action, tool or other problem is named.
2. **The state does not hold.** `find_storage_charges` gives bushels on hand 57300 − 648 − 0 = 56652;
   `find_storage_agreements` gives `reserved_bushels` 54000.0 against `warehouse_receipt_number`
   `WR-004182`; free = **2652**. The programme's load-out minimum is **5000 bushels**
   (`loadout_minimums_notice_and_truck_charges_6e2b98d3`, "Posted load-out terms"). 2652 < 5000.
3. **Finding the write that brings it about, in the words the records and the sentence use.** The
   sentence and the records speak of bushels *pledged against an outstanding warehouse receipt*
   (`reserved_bushels`, `warehouse_receipt_number`). Searching those words reaches
   *"Reducing an Outstanding Warehouse Receipt Over Stored Grain"*
   (`reducing_an_outstanding_warehouse_receipt_ea62d0b3`), whose own rule is *"The revised pledged
   figure is worked out at the desk and then written onto the agreement, so that the receipt stands
   against the quantity stated and the rest of the grain comes back to being free to move."* That is
   the write that raises the free figure. Its own tool is named in its own invocation block and nowhere
   else.
4. After the reduction free = 55632.26 − 27930 = 27702.26 ≥ 5000, so the state holds and P0 unblocks.

**Hop P0 → P2 — `state-derived`.**

1. The blocked policy's second rule: *"The bushels an order releases are fixed only after the storage
   account carries a shrink line raised no earlier than the most recent conditioning charge standing on
   it."*, restated in the same document: *"Until the most recent shrink line on the storage account
   stands no earlier in date than the most recent conditioning charge on it, the quantity an order
   releases is not yet fixed either. Both readings are taken from the records as they stand."*
2. **The state does not hold.** The account's most recent `storage_drying_charged` row is dated
   **2026-01-14**; its only `storage_shrink_taken` row is dated **2025-10-21**, which is earlier.
3. **The write that brings it about.** The sentence's words are *shrink line* on the *storage account*;
   the records call the row a shrink adjustment with `points_removed` and `shrink_bushels`. Those words
   reach *"Conditioning Shrink Taken Against Bushels Held in Store"*
   (`conditioning_shrink_against_bushels_in_store_8d1e5f40`): *"The line the desk records names the
   bushels the shrink was worked out on, the points of moisture it covers and the bushels taken off, and
   those bushels come off what the account shows in store from that moment."*

**Hop P2 → P3 — `state-derived`.**

1. The blocked policy's own rule: *"The bushels taken off for shrink are fixed only after the storage
   account carries a conditioning charge raised on the day the bushels are taken off, since the shrink
   follows the pass that caused it."*, restated in the same form: *"The quantity to be taken off is not
   yet fixed while the storage account for that day carries no conditioning charge; once a conditioning
   charge stands on the account bearing the same date as the shrink line, the quantity is fixed and the
   line is taken."*

### The two differing numbers

Both trace to **one arithmetic slip of the auditor's own, not to any document**. Having worked the
revised pledge to 27930, I wrote that 27930 "already stands on a whole hundred" and left it. It does
not: 27930 carried up to the next whole hundred is **28000**. The rule I applied is the one the
document states, and the document states it correctly and with its own boundary note —
`round_lots_on_a_revised_pledge_2fb6d94c`: *"Where one receipt has been issued against the agreement in
the last twelve months, it is carried up to the next whole hundred bushels"*, and *"Carrying up is
always upward: a figure already standing on a whole thousand is left as it is under the first line, and
a figure already standing on a whole hundred is left as it is under the second."* The source reaches
28000 by the same sentence from the same raw 27930.

With the pledge corrected to 28000 my own method yields, without any other change: bushels free =
55632.26 − 28000 = 27632.26; less the same three holdbacks (1500 + 400 + 800) = 24932.26; the smallest
of 30000, 24932.26 and the 28000 rail ceiling = 24932.26; carried down to a whole multiple of 1000 =
**24000.00** — exactly the source's figure. Every factor tier, every input row, every ordering and
every other argument matched on the first reading.

Per this skill's discipline an arithmetic slip is not a defect of the artefacts, and the `blind_answer`
is left exactly as it was frozen. What the blind answer establishes is unaffected: the visible corpus
alone yields the source's method, tiers, tool sequence, owners and arguments for all four writes.

### The two boundaries the blind answer flagged as open

Both were resolved by the source in favour of the reading the blind answer took, and both are carried
into `policy_kb/grain_storage_desk/1.md` as precision findings rather than runtime failures:

1. **"the bushels applied"** — the source computes `XSUM('grain','grain_ledger','net_bushels', …)`, i.e.
   **net 11200**, as the blind answer assumed. No document names gross or net; the record carries both.
2. **"the bushels the receipt covers"** — the source computes the margin off `pledged_now`, i.e. the
   **54000** standing on the record, as the blind answer assumed.

**Verdict: KB-RUNTIME PASS.** The visible KB never supports waiting or refusing where the source writes;
it offers no second formula, object, action or terminal state; every conclusion was reachable without
the hidden compute, the GT or the raw `initial_state`; every declared prerequisite was carried and every
declared factor was both present and reachable from the records.

## revision_2 — ruling on F2 (unique solvability of "the bushels applied")

Raised by the coordinator on 2026-09-18 after revision 1 was delivered: does F2 leave task 1 with a
second defensible answer? Nothing above is altered; the `blind_answer` and the revision-1
`gt_comparison` stand as frozen.

**Ruling: it does not. Unique solvability holds. KB-RUNTIME PASS stands for task 1.** This is the
thinnest margin in the corpus, and the ground it rests on is narrower than F1's, so I set it out in full.

**The rival reading, and what it costs.** Sum `gross_bushels` rather than `net_bushels` over the
delivery entries applied to a contract in the window: 11350 instead of 11200. Consequence, worked
through:

| | bushels applied | commitment holdback | raw pledge | pledge written | bushels free | releasable | release |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| net (source, and my blind reading) | 11200 | 800 | 27930 | **28000.00** | 27632.26 | 24932.26 | **24000.00** |
| gross (rival) | 11350 | 650 | 27780 | 27800.00 | 27832.26 | 25132.26 | 25000.00 |

Two scored values move. So the question is not academic.

**What does not exclude it.** I checked for an F1-style record discriminator and there is none:

- No seeded row on this agreement was produced by either factor that reads this quantity, so no recorded
  value replays the calculation. There is no prior pledge reduction and no prior drying allowance.
- The contract arithmetic does not adjudicate either: `GC-121773` carries `contracted_bushels` 40000 and
  `open_bushels` 12000, implying 28000 applied in total, while the ledger returns a single
  `contract_application` row of 11350 gross / 11200 net. Neither figure reconciles with 28000, so the
  open position cannot be used to back out which field the rule reads.
- The other factor reading the same quantity, `drying_allowance_for_committed_grain_1f47d0a5`, clears its
  10000 threshold on both figures, so it raises no contradiction either.
- No storage document defines gross or net, and none names a field.

So the rival is **not** excluded by any sentence of the corpus and **not** by any recorded value.

**What does exclude it: the business term the sentence uses, against the record's own field names.**
`bushels_held_for_a_marketing_commitment_41d8c72b` asks for *"the bushels **applied** to the member's
contracts over the last three months, taken from the delivery entries in that product's ledger **that
were applied to a contract**"*, and its ladder turns on *"bushels have been applied to them in the last
three months"*. The row a rollout receives from `find_grain_ledger_entries` names the two quantities by
exactly that distinction and labels itself with the event:

```
{'event_type': 'grain_delivery_applied', 'disposition': 'contract_application',
 'gross_bushels': 11350.0, 'net_bushels': 11200.0, 'delivery_date': '2026-02-06'}
```

`gross_bushels` is the gross weigh; `net_bushels` is the quantity that went to the contract. The rule
names its input by what was done to the bushels — they were *applied* — and the record carries exactly
one field for the applied quantity and one for the gross weigh. Summing the gross where the rule asks
for what was applied is not a second reading of the rule; it is reading a different quantity than the
one the rule names. I took net blind, without hesitation, and flagged F2 only as a precision concern
precisely because the two are not equally reasonable.

**Why this is not the sibling difficulties' defect class.** On the criterion I offer for consistency —
*does something a rollout can actually see separate the readings?* — the answer here is yes, but it is
a **field name matching the business term the sentence uses**, not a sentence and not a recorded value.
The rule sentence does entail a single reading; what it omits is the field name, and the skill is
explicit that an unstated source formulation is not an omission unless the semantics stop being
entailed. The semantics *"the quantity applied to the contract"* is entailed and the record supplies the
mapping. If the sibling sentences instead admit two readings **on their face**, with nothing in prose or
record leaning either way, they are a genuinely different case and the different verdicts are deliberate
rather than an inconsistency.

**What F2 remains, and what I would want the coordinator to weigh.** A precision gap: two factor
documents name their input by a business term that two record fields both plausibly answer to, the
source pins one of them in `compute`, and the corpus never says which. It is the one place in these two
tasks where I would not be surprised to see a competent rollout diverge, and the divergence would move
two scored values. It does not defeat unique solvability on my reading, so it does not change the
verdict; if the coordinator's tolerance for that margin is lower than mine, F2 is the item to act on,
and the remedy lies on the source side (have the prose name the quantity it reads), never in this audit.

**Task 1 verdicts after this revision: runtime blind audit PASS, full-domain two-way scan PASS,
dependency-form scan PASS — unchanged.**
